key_insight: Multimorbidity patterns can be grouped into 16 functional units, and diseases linked to more units tend to have steeper age-related incidence, suggesting shared genetic architecture across chronic disease.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help identify disease pathways and drug-targetable biology that underlie multiple chronic conditions, but it is not yet a clinical decision tool.
method: Analyzed linked health records from UK Biobank across 232 diagnoses in 502,355 participants.
Used generative representation learning to derive 16 functional units from pre-assessment disease co-occurrence.
Compared each diagnosis’s functional-unit breadth with later incidence and validated genetic signals in FinnGen and the Million Veteran Program.
evidence_signal: The association between functional-unit breadth and age-dependent incidence was moderate to strong (Spearman rho = 0.50 overall; 0.46 among diagnoses with rising hazards), and GWAS identified 34 regions missed by comparator analyses.
watch_item: The findings are observational and population-based, so they need external validation before being used to guide prediction, diagnosis, or treatment.
paper_title: Functional organization of multimorbidity links chronic disease incidence to shared genetic architecture
